caption: The drawing depicts a wrought iron gate or decorative grill, consisting of vertical bars connected by two horizontal support bars at the top and bottom, as well as shorter horizontal bars at both ends. The grill has a symmetrical design with intricate curling and fleur-de-lis-like ornamental elements, especially noticeable at the top center and distributed evenly along the vertical bars, where two pairs of curvilinear flourishes are attached to each bar. The entire structure is rendered in shades of brown to black, suggesting aged or rusted iron, with faint hand-drawn lines indicating shadows and dimensionality. The background is a plain off-white or beige, and no other objects or details are present in the image, except for the artist’s signature "Geoffrey Holt" at the lower right corner.
title: Iron Grille (at Window) a Restoration Drawing
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
